title: aether_converter ingest job
description: Job consumed by `aether_converter ingest --job-file <json>`. The file may be a single job object OR a JSON array of job objects (batch). Authoritative source: crates/aether_converter/src/ingest.rs (IngestJob). Contract v2.0: terrain inputs are the `sources` array; `base_tif`/`swiss_tifs` are deprecated aliases.

buildings_pbf_list.description: The single-job form refuses buildings_pbf_list (batch only, changelog 51).

path.description: GeoTIFF or .abt tile to sample; the two are told apart by the AETH magic, never by extension. A GeoTIFF must carry a geotransform (ModelTransformation, or ModelTiepoint+ModelPixelScale); a file without one is a hard error — georeferencing is never derived from file names. An .abt source is self-describing: geometry from its 44-byte header (geographic WGS84 degrees; the legacy span-in-scale_x header quirk is corrected), R16SINT (version 1) only, values already i16 half-metres loaded raw, stride padding stripped, -9999 voids pass through; a truncated/corrupt header is a hard error naming the file.

crs.description: "EPSG:nnnn" or a proj string starting with '+'. Optional: when absent the converter reads the GeoTIFF's GeoKeyDirectory (ProjectedCSTypeGeoKey 3072, else GeographicTypeGeoKey 2048); an absent or user-defined (32767) key is a hard error naming the file. Geographic CRSs are sampled directly as lon/lat degrees; projected CRSs are sampled through a WGS84->source transform. Setting crs on an .abt source is a hard error (abt sources are self-describing).

nodata.description: No-data value in source units. Optional: when absent the GeoTIFF's GDAL_NODATA ascii tag applies (if present). Matching samples become the -9999 void sentinel at load time. Setting nodata on an .abt source is a hard error (abt sources are self-describing; their voids are already -9999).

format.description: Tile payload format; defaults to r16sint behavior when absent.

resolution_m.description: Metres per pixel. Sources finer than this are area-averaged over each output pixel's footprint (no-data excluded from the mean); a source at or coarser than this is taken as-is, never interpolated. See CONTRACT.md section 6.

sources.description: Prioritised terrain inputs: array order is priority, first source with a valid sample wins per pixel. Mutually exclusive with the deprecated base_tif/swiss_tifs — supplying both is a hard error.

void_fill_m.description: Optional. A pixel no source covers is written as round(void_fill_m * 2) half-metres (saturating i16) instead of the -9999 void sentinel. Buildings rasterize after, unchanged. Absent keeps the sentinel.

base_tif.description: DEPRECATED (contract v2.0): alias for a trailing sources[] entry with crs "EPSG:4326". Accepted for older callers; slated for removal in the next major version. Do not combine with sources.

swiss_tifs.description: DEPRECATED (contract v2.0): alias for leading sources[] entries with crs "EPSG:2056" (in order). Accepted for older callers; slated for removal in the next major version. Do not combine with sources. No longer required.

buildings_file.description: FlatGeobuf building footprints to burn in: one .fgb, or a directory of them (a directory holding no .fgb is a hard error). Height follows the shared building height ladder, first finite strictly-positive value wins: (1) geometry Z, read as an ABSOLUTE roof elevation in metres above mean sea level, where the geometry carries Z; (2) attribute height / render_height / building:height, in that order, as metres ABOVE GROUND; (3) attribute levels / building:levels / building_levels, in that order, x 3.0 m per storey, as metres ABOVE GROUND; (4) a 6.0 m default, ABOVE GROUND. Rungs 2-4 are never absolute - an above-ground height is resolved against the terrain under its own footprint before it is written. Attribute values are text: the leading decimal number is taken and any suffix ignored, so "12", "12.5" and "12 m" read alike; zero, negative and unparseable values fall through to the next rung. A source that cannot be opened, parsed or scanned fails the run (message contains 'failed to apply buildings' and 'refusing to write a building-less tile') rather than warning and writing a building-less tile. Every burn prints one '[Buildings]' line per tile to stdout, including the case where nothing was drawn.

buildings_pbf_dir.description: Directory of {z}_{x}_{y}.pbf vector tiles (gzip or plain) to burn in. Vector tiles carry no geometry Z, so height starts at rung 2 of the same ladder as buildings_file - height / render_height / building:height, then levels / building:levels / building_levels x 3.0 m, then a 6 m default - and is always read as above-ground. All tiles must share one zoom level. A batch decodes it once, before its first tile - with buildings_pbf_ready and the marker missing at launch, once the marker appears (changelog 48).

buildings_pbf_ready.description: Batch ingest only (a JSON array of jobs): file name inside buildings_pbf_dir (e.g. "_ready") whose existence declares the directory complete, so a caller can fetch the building tiles WHILE the batch samples its terrain - the download job's hand-over (CONTRACT 9b, changelog 45), same name rules and messages. A batch looks for <buildings_pbf_dir>/<buildings_pbf_ready> as a file at launch: there -> the directory is decoded at once, exactly as without the field. Missing -> every tile's terrain starts at once, the marker is looked for every 250 ms (the directory need not exist at launch) and the directory is decoded when it appears, with the usual decode lines; a tile whose terrain is done before the building set is decoded is HELD in memory (not written) up to buildings_hold_mb, a tile past that waits on its worker thread; once decoded, the held tiles are burnt and written in the order they finished, every later tile inline. stdout gets `[Buildings] waiting for the building tiles (<path>)` when the first tile has to wait, then `[Buildings] building tiles ready after <s.s> s` and `[Buildings] <n> tile(s) held (<m.m> MB) until the building tiles were ready` (+ `; <k> more waited on their worker threads (hold budget <b.b> MB full)`). Same .abt bytes as a batch whose directory was complete at launch. A marker still missing after buildings_pbf_wait_s, or a directory that does not decode, fails the batch (`Building tiles not ready: ...` / the decode's error, exit 1) with no tile of that directory written. Requires buildings_pbf_dir; must be one plain file name (no / or \, not . or ..) and not a {z}_{x}_{y}.pbf/.mvt tile name; the jobs naming one buildings_pbf_dir must give the same buildings_pbf_ready and buildings_pbf_wait_s - else the batch fails before any tile. A single job (a JSON object) refuses the field. Absent or null: unchanged. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.12 (older builds ignore it and read the directory at launch: fail when it does not exist yet, or burn what it holds then); CONTRACT 9a, changelog 48.

buildings_pbf_wait_s.description: Seconds a batch waits for buildings_pbf_ready - or (aether_converter >= 0.2.14, changelog 51) for the buildings_pbf_list file - counted from its first look at launch; absent or null = 1800. Read only together with buildings_pbf_ready or buildings_pbf_list (alone it changes nothing, and is not checked); outside 0..86400 the batch fails before any tile. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.12; CONTRACT 9a, changelog 48.

buildings_hold_mb.description: Megabytes (MiB) of finished tiles (size_px^2 x 2 bytes each) a batch may hold in memory while it waits for buildings_pbf_ready; a tile that does not fit waits on its worker thread, which starts no other tile meanwhile. The batch's budget is the smallest value its watched jobs give, taken as given (0 holds nothing). Absent on all of them: half of the available memory left after the worker pool's own reservation (threads x the per-tile estimate + the 192 MB chunk cache), at most 4096 MB, never below one tile. Read only together with buildings_pbf_ready or (>= 0.2.14) buildings_pbf_list; outside 0..1048576 the batch fails before any tile. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.12; CONTRACT 9a, changelog 48.

buildings_pbf_list.description: Batch ingest only (a JSON array of jobs): the ABSOLUTE path of a UTF-8 text file naming, one per line, the building tile files of buildings_pbf_dir this job burns ({z}_{x}_{y}.pbf or .mvt, the name only; lines end in \n or \r\n; blank lines, lines starting with #, blanks around a name and a byte-order mark ignored; a name listed twice is decoded once). Only the listed files are read - buildings_pbf_dir is never listed, so it may be a store of far more tiles - in name order, by the directory's loader: the .abt bytes and lines of the same batch whose buildings_pbf_dir holds exactly the listed tiles, except the decode's start line `[Rust] Decoding <n> listed building tiles from "<dir>" (once for the run)...` (<n> the distinct listed names, <dir> as the job gives it). The file is the ready signal: missing when the batch looks, it is waited for exactly as buildings_pbf_ready's marker (watcher every 250 ms, buildings_pbf_wait_s, buildings_hold_mb, `[Buildings] waiting for the building tiles (<list path>)` / `building tiles ready after <s.s> s` / held line; never coming: `Building tiles not ready: the list file <list path> (buildings_pbf_list) ...`, exit 1, no tile of it written); write it last, under another name, then rename it into place. An empty list (no byte, or blank/comment lines only) decodes nothing, as an empty directory. A listed tile not in buildings_pbf_dir (or unreadable) fails the batch: `Building tile <name> listed in <list> is not in <dir>`; a line with a path separator, or no tile name, fails it naming the line. Requires buildings_pbf_dir, which must exist when the batch starts; excludes buildings_pbf_ready; must be absolute; jobs naming one list must give the same buildings_pbf_dir and buildings_pbf_wait_s - else the batch fails before any tile. A single job (a JSON object) refuses the field. Absent or null: unchanged. Additive, aether_converter >= 0.2.14 (older builds ignore it and decode the whole buildings_pbf_dir at launch, without waiting); CONTRACT 9a, changelog 51.
